chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Sitting in once with Duke Ellington's band in Chicago
summary: His only time with Duke, at the Audubon Ballroom, with Sonny Greer still on drums.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you ever get to work with Duke as a sub. Like Panama apparently did for like a very short time.
No, I never had the pleasure, one time had the pleasure of sitting in with Duke's band, that was in

Chicago; we was playing the Regal Theatre and I think they were playing the Audubon Ballroom right next to the Regal or something, and we had finished the theatre, which is about 11:00, 11:30, well next door with them playing a dance, they had to play until about 1, 1:30. Everybody out of Cab's band went over to hear Duke and then night I sit in with Duke's band which was about the last set, and that's my only time ever playing with Duke.
That's when Sonny Greer was still--
Sonny was still with the band, mm hmm.
Did you get a charge out of that?

Oh yeah, oh God, yeah, I just loved sitting in there with Duke. Was the last set, you know, they had closed the books and was probably just a lot of those numbers that I knew, like 'Take the A Train' and all those things you know, heads, and just sitting down there and play them. That was my only time ever playing with Duke. I loved that band, though, playing with the band. There was Tizol and Barney and all the guys, Lawrence Brown, everybody.
